QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_9

question.text: Ujala Solar Pvt Ltd claims its off-grid solar lamps created 5,000 new jobs in rural Bihar. The SIA discovers that 1,500 of those jobs came at the direct expense of local kerosene retailers who closed down. In SROI, how should the 1,500 jobs be treated?

answer.text: Added as additional positive outcome — job creation is always positive
Treated as displacement — deducted from gross outcome because the job was transferred from one group to another, not net-new
Treated as drop-off — because kerosene retailers dropped out
Treated as deadweight — because the market would have shifted anyway

explanation.text: The Logic: Displacement is the portion of outcome produced at the expense of another group. The 1,500 kerosene-retailer jobs lost offset the solar-related jobs gained — they are not net-new social value and must be deducted from gross outcome in the SROI calculation. The Trap: Adding is wrong because it double-counts. Drop-off is temporal fade, not substitution. Deadweight is the without-intervention baseline. Displacement uniquely captures the 'one group gains, another loses' dynamic. Cross-Exam Context: X-A IA discusses crowding-out effects in policy; XIX AIF references negative externalities. XXIII's displacement is the SROI-specific application of the same idea. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Displacement assessment requires field work with losing-side stakeholders — interview kerosene retailers, not just solar beneficiaries, or you'll miss the offset and over-state the SROI.
